Sunday Guardian Live Who is Josh Kerr? British Athlete Shatters Men’s Mile World Record at London Diamond League 2026 Josh Kerr rewrote history at the London Diamond League 2026 by breaking the men’s mile world record with a stunning time of 3:42.66. The British middle-distance star eclipsed Hicham El Guerrouj’s long-standing mark, adding another milestone to a career that already includes World Championship gold and Olympic medals. By: Arpan Mondal Last Updated: July 19, 2026 00:12:51 IST Who is Josh Kerr? British Athlete Shatters Men's Mile World Record at London Diamond League 2026 (Image Source: X) 116 British Athlete Josh Kerr lit up the London Diamond League 2026, shattering the men’s mile world record in style. In front of a massive home crowd, Kerr breached the finishing line in three minutes 42.66 seconds to beat Morocco’s Hicham El Guerrouj’s mark that had prevailed for 27 years. It was not a fluke performance by the 28-year-old, who earlier revealed his aim of owning the world record, or let’s say, manifested it. The dream came true at the home Diamond League amid a buzzing London Stadium packed with 60,000 spectators. Josh Kerr World Record When Hicham El Guerrouj set the previous World Record for Morocco in 1999, Josh Kerr was only one year old. Now, after nearly three decades, he bettered the Moroccan’s finish by almost half a second. Kerr appeared at the London Diamond League as the sixth-fastest man in the world, holding the British mile record of 3:45.34. With his historic show in London, Kerr, a five-time global medallist, became only the seventh athlete from Great Britain to claim the mile world record.
